title: Between the Monthly Meetings: What a Fractional CFO Actually Does
linkedin:
Most owners judge a fractional CFO by the monthly meeting. Report lands, questions get asked, actions get agreed, done until next month.

That meeting is not the engagement. It is the summary of three or four weeks of work that already happened before anyone sat down.

Behind it sits a rhythm: a weekly check on the cash position against the forecast, a KPI dashboard kept current rather than three weeks stale, a mid-month question modelled properly instead of decided on gut feel, and material prepared ahead of a lender or board conversation so the owner walks in with a position, not a hope.

None of it replaces the bookkeeper or compliance accountant, who keep the ledger accurate and the lodgements on time. It sits on top of that work, turning clean numbers into decisions made a month or two earlier than they otherwise would be.

The real value of a fractional CFO is not the meeting. It is the continuity. A CFO who has been watching the numbers weekly will typically notice a shift in debtor days or a margin slide two months before it would show up in a quarterly review, simply because they were already looking when it started.

For most owner-led businesses, that earlier decision is worth more than any single report.

A question we hear a lot from business owners across Brisbane, the Gold Coast and further along the East Coast: what does a fractional CFO actually do outside the one meeting a month?

The honest answer is that most of the useful work happens in the weeks between meetings, not during them. That includes checking the cash position against the forecast every week or fortnight, keeping a KPI dashboard current so the numbers that matter are never more than a few days old, working through a decision an owner is weighing before it gets made on gut feel, and preparing properly ahead of any conversation with a bank or board.

None of this replaces the relationship a business already has with its bookkeeper or accountant, who keep the compliance side accurate and on time. It sits on top of that work, turning clean numbers into decisions made earlier than they otherwise would be.

If you have ever wondered what you would actually be paying for with a fractional CFO, this is it. Read the full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.
